score_breakdown.design_fidelity: 7/10. What section M5.5 specifies is implemented as written: the body form of the plan intent with the client pos ignored, stop at standoff_km on the approach line at the body's position at arrival, flyby at exactly b on the clock_deg side with a run-out of dBurn + 1e6 km, the 12-step intercept on planBurnCoastBurn.galaxyTime, the five refusals plus out_of_range and no_converge, additive protocol fields gated on the minor, old-message tests unmodified. -2 for the stale_plan rule (navigation.ail:267, core.ail:276): a body plan is refused at commit unless the Earth clock has not moved since the plan. D-12 fixes the host clock at one ship-day per real second at rest (ui/galaxy_map.gd:35, HOST_DTAU on every planning tick, :510) and makes the commit a 1.5 s hold that 'cannot commit in a single frame' (ui/galaxy_map.gd:41-45), so through the existing map flow every body commit would be stale_plan; the design's G2 ('sees the plan ... commits') cannot be met by a Godot-only M5.6a without pausing the clock (against D-12) or guessing plan_id and bundling plan+commit (which hides the plan). The rule is deterministic and conservative, so it is not wrong, but the sim needs a re-plan-at-commit path (keep the BodyReq in NavPlan; at commit re-run planBody at the current t, commit the fresh plan, refuse only if it is refused), and nothing schedules that. -1 for ring_crossing (navigation.ail:183-189) implementing the design's letter ('crosses a ring plane') and therefore missing a leg that lies in the plane: my probe starts 3 R and 10 R from Saturn in its ring plane (height 3.5e-8 km) and plans a stop at 1.1 R + bubble; the plan is accepted ('ok') although the leg runs through the A, B and C rings in-plane (den < 1e-12 -> 'no crossing' at :187, and for a nearly in-plane leg s falls outside [0, legKm]). Reachable in play after a stop at Titan (inclination 0.3 deg). The check already has the host's nearest approach; refusing when that approach is inside the outer ring and within a ring half-thickness of the plane closes it. Not deducted but recorded: body arrivals run M4's `arrive` (core.ail:446-460): a stop at Mars logs 'arrival' and 'news' with starId 'mars', draws from the news stream and sets a tier-0 Earth-news item after a 26-day trip; this is explicitly deferred in the sprint JSON notes, but once M5.5b's Sol tour golden is recorded the news-stream draw sequence is frozen into the replay bytes, so it should be settled in M5.5b, not after. Open choices judged sensible: safety minimum 1.1 R + bubble (Jupiter's 1 mbar level is 0.4 % of R; the bubble is 100 m) and the 0.1 AU clamp (the design says 'between the safety minimum and 0.1 AU'; clamping rather than refusing is a fair reading, the test pins it); clock_deg: 0 = pole projected across the approach line, 90 = cross(u, north) = right of the body as seen from the ship, verified in the ring plane at 90 (dot with the pole < 1e-3), coherent with the design's '0 = north, measured around the approach line'; the hello split by minor is a wart with a real reason (the x86_64 goldens embed the hello line; replay.py normalises only the minor) and should be removed the next time the goldens are regenerated, when minors 0-3 should report the pin too.

physics_verification.oracle_saturn_flyby_0p5c_b_3R: Pass time planner = oracle to the last bit (0.000273653467758866 yr, 8,635.8 s after departure; the trip is 2.41 h Earth time; Saturn moves 86,684 km = 1.44 R by the pass, so the intercept matters). Leg 1,295,734,114.844249 km, rel diff 0; arrival point |planner - oracle| = 0 km; galaxyTime rel 2e-16, shipTime rel 3e-16; fellBack false both. Pass geometry: |Q - B(tp)| = 180,804.000000024 km, (Q - B).(Q - x0) = 38 km^2 on a 1.3e9 km leg (float64 rounding), so the closest approach is b to 2.4e-8 km against the moving planet. D at pass 1.1547005383792 = gamma(0.5c): correct, the pass is at theta_rest = 90 deg so D = gamma(1 + beta cos 90) = gamma, which equals 1/(gamma(1 - beta cos theta')) at the aberrated angle cos theta' = beta.
physics_verification.oracle_io_stop_0p001c: Arrival time planner - oracle = 4.4e-10 s on a 26.49-day trip; leg 686,264,057.276331 km rel diff 0; arrival point |planner - oracle| = 6e-8 km; |arrival - Io(tA)| = the stand-off (18,294 km = 10.04 R_Io) to 1e-6 km. Io moves 31.2 million km during the leg (1,706 stand-offs), so aiming at Io's position at t0 would miss by 1,700 stand-offs: the intercept is essential and correct.
physics_verification.light_time_and_frame: The planner evaluates bodyAt at galaxy (coordinate) time, c.t0 = ship.motion.t (core.ail:244) plus the package's trip.galaxyTime or motionAt(...).t (navigation.ail:116-117, 127-128, 160-161): the intercept is solved in Earth time with the ship's coordinate arrival time, in the frame where the bodies are at rest to 2e-4 c. It uses the geometric (instantaneous) position, which is right for navigation: the ship must be where the body is at arrival, not where its light shows it; the retarded position belongs to the view (systemAt, M5.1b) and is not used here. intercept.pos on the wire is the geometric position at arrival and the design describes it as such.
physics_verification.closest_approach_and_clock: At 0.5c the body's own motion shifts the true closest approach by 2.4e-8 km (negligible). At the slowest allowed pass (Mars at 0.001c, b = 10,000 km) the true closest approach to the moving planet is 9,999.089 km, 0.43 s after the nominal pass: 0.9 km (0.01 %) under b. Harmless (1.1 R + bubble keeps 10 % of R in hand) and noted so M5.5b's AC17 '1 km' tolerance is not surprised at low speed.
physics_verification.gate3_package_only: navigation.ail restates no trip formula: trips come from planBurnCoastBurn (navigation.ail:103), times along the leg from motionAt by 64-step bisection on x (109-117), beta from betaOf, D from optics.doppler, the braking distance from the package's dBurn (165). The oracle's independent closed forms agree with the package to 2e-16, which is the check that nothing was restated wrongly.

findings.issue: stale_plan refuses a body commit at any Earth time other than the planning tick. D-12 runs the host clock at rest on every tick (HOST_DTAU) and makes the commit a 1.5 s hold, so the existing plan -> confirm -> commit flow would refuse every body plan. M5.6a is planned as Godot-only.
findings.suggestion: Keep the BodyReq in NavPlan; at commit of a body plan re-run planBody at the current t and commit the fresh plan (refuse only if the fresh plan is refused). Deterministic, replays from the same input log, and lets the player look at the plan while the planet moves. Schedule it in M5.5b or M5.6a's sim half.

findings.issue: ring_crossing only tests the point where the leg crosses the ring plane. A leg lying in (or nearly in) the plane inside the outer ring is accepted: probe from 3 R and 10 R in Saturn's ring plane to a stop at 1.1 R + bubble -> ok, through the A, B and C rings. Reachable after a stop at Titan (i = 0.3 deg).
findings.suggestion: Also refuse when the host's nearest approach (already computed) is inside ringKm and the leg's height above the plane at that point is below a ring half-thickness (e.g. 1,000 km, or the bubble).

findings.issue: A body arrival runs M4's `arrive`: 'arrival' and 'news' log rows with starId 'mars', a news-stream draw and a tier-0 Earth-news item for a 26-day hop. Deferred in the sprint JSON notes only.
findings.suggestion: Gate `arrive` on `plan.nav == None` (or log a 'stop' kind without a news draw) in M5.5b, before the Sol tour golden freezes the news-stream sequence; add the item to the plan's M5.5b row.

findings.issue: The hello reports relativity 0.4.0 below minor 4 and the real pin from minor 4. Reason given (x86_64 goldens embed the hello line) is real; the split is a wart.
findings.suggestion: When the goldens are next regenerated, report relativityPin() at every minor and drop the split; until then the comment and make hello-pin suffice.

findings.issue: Four evaluator mutants survive: Doppler direction sign at the pass, the bubble in the collision margin, the D > 2b flyby bound, moon target.index.
findings.suggestion: Assert Io's index (10) in the stop fixture; a collision fixture at R + bubble +- 1 km; a flyby fixture at D just above/below 2b; the Doppler sign can be pinned with a short run-out so the pass falls in the brake and theta_rest != 90.

findings.issue: At the slowest pass (0.001c) the true closest approach to the moving body is 0.01 % under b (Mars: 0.9 km on 10,000 km); at 0.5c it is 2e-8 km.
findings.suggestion: No change; note for M5.5b's AC17 tolerance at low speed.
